extracted.intended_audience: vocational education administrators and faculty; workshop organizers; state bureau staff involved in proposal-development training
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and running a multi-day workshop to teach vocational educators how to prepare fundable project proposals, including identifying problems, learning funding sources/VEIN, writing objectives, developing prospectuses, and receiving individual assistance. Also guidance on selecting participants and structuring sessions for maximum productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and define the problem to be studied
rubrics_metrics.description: To help participants identify and define the problem - to be studied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshop objective #1. The report emphasizes that many vocational educators have ideas but need help turning them into a clearly defined problem suitable for a proposal. In practice the workshop assisted only five participants to develop a prospectus; selection should favor those who already have an idea or can demonstrate ability to define a problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform participants of funding sources (State, Federal, Private)
rubrics_metrics.description: To inform participants of funding sources interested in their problem area (State, Federal, and Private).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshop objective #2. Guidance notes that vocational educators often lack thorough knowledge of programs (e.g., Vocational Education Amendments of 1968) and of other federal agencies, business/industry, and foundations as potential funders; teaching about these sources should be part of the curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach existence and proper utilization of VEIN
rubrics_metrics.description: To inform participants of the existence and proper utilization of the Vocational Education Information Network (VEIN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshop objective #3. VEIN instruction (presented by Miss Erma Keyes) was well received; participants were impressed that information could be obtained easily. Teaching how to use VEIN is an explicit component of effective proposal-preparation training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach essential components/anatomy of a proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: To inform participants of the essential components of a proposal (the anatomy of a proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshop objective #4 and scheduled sessions (e.g., 'anatomy of a proposal', 'proposal writing'). Practical instruction should cover required sections and typical expectations of funders so participants can assemble a complete proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assist participants in writing a high-quality proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist participants in the writing of a high quality proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshop objective #5. The program used individual conferences and critique sessions; outcomes were measured by creation of prospectuses (one excellent, one good, three fair). Hands-on assistance and individualized feedback are critical to producing fundable proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide assistance in writing objectives, project design, and measurement of outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: To expedite the proposal writing by providing assistance in the areas of writing objectives, design of project and measurement of outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshop objective #6. Includes specific instruction (e.g., sessions on writing behavioral objectives, small-group practice). The report highlights the behavioral objectives session as particularly beneficial for curricular and proposal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a mixed structure: presentations, small groups, individual conferences, and critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the workshop with morning informational presentations and afternoon individual conferences, plus small/large group sessions and critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described in Procedures and the Schedule of Activities. The recommended mix includes expert presentations (funding programs, VEIN), needs assessment, small-group practice on objectives, and individual conferences by arrangement; final critique sessions are used to improve prospectuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select participants based on submitted idea and ability to write
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants should be selected on the basis of the idea which they present and upon their ability within their organization to write a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation section: selecting participants who already want to develop a proposal and can work within their organizational context increases workshop effectiveness. The Bureau should assist in identifying and selecting these participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit participant numbers to assure individual attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps the number of participants might be reduced to assure individual attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation section: fewer participants allow more intensive, individualized assistance, increasing the chance that prospective projects advance to fundable proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance planning, advertising, and bureau responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A workshop of this nature should be well advertised and pushed by the Bureau; the Bureau should have responsibility for identifying and selecting participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation section: better preplanning and active promotion by the Bureau of Vocational, Technical and Continuing Education will improve recruitment of appropriate participants and overall success of the workshop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include sessions on needs assessment and consortium/cooperative arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include instruction on needs assessment, consortium and cooperative arrangements, and how the system works and prospectus development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule entries (Dr. Higgins on needs assessment and consortiums; sessions on how the system works and development of a prospectus). These topics help participants situate projects in broader programmatic and partnership contexts that funders favor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate informally via individual discussions and by measuring outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation should involve informal discussion with each participant to assess needs and help develop ideas; evaluate outputs such as prospectuses and participant satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation section: the workshop used informal, participant-by-participant discussion to assess needs and measure outcomes (prospectus quality rated excellent/good/fair). Follow-up contact with authors of strong prospectuses indicates potential for later funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize behavioral objectives writing as a core skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing behavioral objectives is an important session and skill that helps both proposal and curriculum development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation and schedule note: five participants reported the behavioral objectives session enabled them to write better curricula and was valuable for proposal development. Small group sessions to practice objectives were part of the schedule.
